 Metals Gold drops 2% to over one-year low as hawkish Fed signals boost dollar
 Published Tue, Nov 17 2026 10:21 PM EST Updated Wed, Nov 18 2026 6:34 AM EST WATCH LIVE In this article
 @GC26Z 
 Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Gold prices fell more than 1% on Wednesday to their lowest level in over a year, as a firmer dollar and expectations of higher U.S. interest rates weighed, while investors awaited minutes from the Federal Reserve's meeting for clues on the policy outlook. Edgar Su | Reuters Gold prices fell more than 2% on Wednesday to their ​lowest level in over ​a year, pressured ​by a firm US dollar and growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will keep raising interest rates after hawkish comments from policymakers.
 Spot gold dropped 2% to $3,772.91 per ounce by 0909 GMT. ⁠It hit $3,757 ‌earlier in the session, its lowest level since September ⁠2025.
 US gold futures for December delivery declined 2.3% to $3,776.10.
 "The strength of the greenback and growing expectations for a hawkish Federal Reserve in the next few months remain on the table, pressuring the ‌gold price," said Carlo Alberto De Casa external analyst for Swissquote.
 The dollar hovered near a 19-month high, making greenback-priced bullion more expensive for buyers ​overseas.
 Fed officials struck a hawkish tone on Tuesday as New York Fed President John Williams said the central bank would likely need to raise rates again to counter inflation pressures, while St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said ⁠several additional rate hikes may be needed to bring inflation under control.
 Markets are currently assigning a ‌97.8% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, ‌and a nearly 2.2% chance of a 50bp hike according to CME's FedWatch tool.
 Higher interest rates raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold, reducing its appeal to investors.
 Investors now await ⁠minutes of the Fed's Oct. 27-28 policy meeting, due at 1900 GMT.
 "The FOMC ⁠meeting minutes may offer further clues about Fed officials' biases during ⁠the previous meeting, and may test the market's current expectations for 3 more rate hikes through mid-2027," said Han Tan, chief market analyst at ​Bybit.
 Spot silver slipped 3.5% to $45.75, after ‌touching its lowest level since October 2025 in the session.
 The global platinum market will swing back to a deficit next year due to higher bar and coin demand and smaller outflows from platinum-backed exchange-traded funds, the World Platinum Investment Council said on Wednesday.
